fullPassage: Imagine two students examining their grades on a math test. One student tries hard but rarely gets a grade higher than a "C." The other is the top math student in the school; she always gets an "A." On this particular test, however, both students receive a "B." These students might use the same words in discussing their grades, but with a remarkably different tone. The first student would likely deliver the sentence "I got a 'B' on the math test" with some surprise and happiness in her voice. She would sound excited and hopeful. The second student's tone would indicate that she was not happy and suggest disappointment or worry. Both students used the same words, but they did not mean the same thing. The different tones mark the differences in the students' feelings.
